top: growth in India's maize area over ten years, to 144 lakh hectares in 2025-26; mustard grew as much.
fall in jowar area over the same decade, the steepest of any major crop.
typical monthly price move in the onion-potato-tomato price cluster, against 3.4% for harvest-bunched field crops such as wheat.

sections.h2: Maize and mustard area grew 64% in ten years, while jowar area fell 42%

chart.title: Maize and mustard gained the most land; jowar lost the most
chart.source: UPAG all-India area, production and yield; this blog's calculations.

sections.means: Land is moving toward crops with new demand or price support and away from the traditional dryland cereals.
sections.todo: Plan inputs, storage and procurement around the crops gaining area, led by maize and mustard.

sections.h2: Maize, groundnut, moong, gram and jowar yields grew 3.4-4.7% a year since 2015

chart.title: Yields of five crops grew 3.4-4.7% a year since 2015; cotton slipped

sections.means: Rice and wheat yields grew about 2% a year, slower than the fastest crops, while tur and soybean have barely moved.
sections.todo: Direct seed and extension effort to tur, soybean and cotton, where yield has barely moved or slipped.

sections.h2: Indo-Gangetic states use 326 kg of urea a hectare against 124 kg in the eastern rice belt

chart.title: Urea use per hectare differs sharply between crop-mix clusters
chart.sub: Urea sold per hectare of cropped land, 2025-26, kg.
chart.source: Department of Fertilizers; UPAG; this blog's calculations.

sections.means: Where urea use is highest, each tonne returns less grain, about 8.6 tonnes against about 12, which fits diminishing returns to nitrogen.
sections.todo: Aim fertiliser-efficiency efforts at the Indo-Gangetic states rather than raising urea supply everywhere.

sections.h2: Tomato, garlic and onion move 13.5-20.4% a month; wheat, maize and soybean 2.5-2.9%

chart.title: Perishables swing 6.2-20.4% a month; wheat, maize and rice 2.3-2.9%
chart.sub: Typical monthly price move, %; the four perishables with the largest moves against four storable grains.

sections.means: Storable grains, pulses and oilseeds move a few percent a month, while vegetables that cannot be stored for long can double or halve within a season.
sections.todo: Build storage and price-stabilisation support around vegetables rather than grains.

details.summary: Seasonal price index, selected readings (1.00 = the crop's average month)
details.html: Onion is cheapest at 0.58 and dearest at 1.60. Potato reads 1.31 in November and 1.04 in December. Garlic reads 0.97 in July and 1.32 in December.
